summary: The implementation generally uses specimens as independent units, preserves nuclei as nested observations, reports effect sizes and uncertainty only when each group has at least three specimens, applies family-specific Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and separates count, sampled area/volume, and density. Acceptance is blocked because the claimed replay PDFs and source artifacts are absent from the reviewed repository, and no automated test verifies numerical agreement across source CSV/JSON, spreadsheets, plots, and PDFs. Therefore the required primary-report agreement criterion cannot be independently verified.

findings.title: Claimed report-to-source agreement is not independently auditable
findings.impact: The acceptance criterion that primary reports agree with source tables cannot be established. Shared in-memory derivation reduces risk but does not detect serialization, worksheet selection, plotting, formatting, stale-artifact, or PDF-label/value discrepancies. A required statistics/reporting check therefore fails and blocks this high-risk production claim.
evidence: V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:61 and V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:92-95 cite a replay directory and four report artifacts that are absent from the reviewed repository.

scripts/generate_v57_biological_comparison.py:1087-1118, 1187-1249, and 1310-1451 create CSV, plot, PDF, and workbook products through different output paths without a numerical cross-format reconciliation test.
tests/test_saturn_v57_multisample.py:907-917 validates workbook structure only, and tests/test_saturn_v57_multisample.py:920-968 validates PDF creation only.
findings.recommendation: Retain or archive a compact acceptance fixture containing source specimen CSV/JSON and generated PDF/XLSX/plot artifacts. Add an automated reconciliation test that extracts or records every displayed primary value and verifies agreement, with documented rounding, among source tables, workbook cells, plotted values, PDF tables/text, and report metadata.

findings.title: Reference-group direction is inferred from label text
findings.impact: Generic labels avoid hard-coded genotype output, but substring-based inference can silently choose the wrong effect direction for unconventional group names, making comparison-minus-reference effects misleading.
evidence: scripts/generate_v57_biological_comparison.py:131-139 chooses the reference by matching control/reference/wild/w1118/WT tokens and otherwise selects the alphabetically first group.
scripts/generate_v57_biological_comparison.py:270-304 and 1316-1319 use that inferred direction in effect estimates and report language.
findings.recommendation: Require an explicit reference-group field in the study manifest or report command, record it in provenance, and fail clearly when it is absent or does not match exactly one group.

limitations: No full image stack was run, as required by the review instructions.
Other reviewers' outputs and the untracked audits/runs/20260821-v571-remediation-acceptance-rc3 directory were not read.
Focused tests could not run because the read-only environment had no writable temporary directory.
Absent replay artifacts prevented direct PDF, spreadsheet, plot, CSV, and JSON value reconciliation.
recommended_follow_up: Add and run a compact cross-format numerical reconciliation test in a writable isolated test environment.
Archive the exact acceptance-candidate replay sources and generated reports at stable repository or release-artifact paths, then perform a superseding statistics-reporting audit.
Replace label-heuristic reference selection with explicit manifest-backed reference-group provenance.
